reviews.text: Amazing place. If you wanna visit this shrine come at early morning or 3 hours before closing. There is many hidden corners where you can sit and chill and feel the atmosphere of place. There are many small buildings which are like small museums. There is also beautiful gardens. Not many English texts. But ticket in advance. It faster. Enjoy you visit.

Summary 4/5: A historical dialogue worth the time—if you pace it right. Wuhou Shrine (武侯祠) is essential for anyone interested in the Three Kingdoms (三国) era, but it works as a peaceful retreat even if you aren't a history buff. It remains unique as the only temple in China where a monarch, Liu Bei (刘备), and his minister, Zhuge Liang (诸葛亮), are enshrined together. The Logistics: * 🚇Getting There: Accessibility is excellent now. Take Metro Line 10 (10号线), alight at the new Wuhouci Station (武侯祠站), and it’s an easy 3-minute walk to the entrance. * 🎟️ Tickets: cost CNY 50 per adult, recommend booking via Trip.com in advance to save time at the gate. The Reality (Learn from my mistake): * 👥 The Crowds: This isn't just a tourist trap; it is incredibly popular with locals and student groups, meaning it gets packed. The energy is vibrant, but it can be overwhelming. * ⏳Time Management: We regret underestimating the crowds and the sheer scale of the grounds. We didn't allocate enough time to truly appreciate the history amidst the flow of people. Don't rush this. The Experience: * 🎍Expand Your Visit: To do this justice, allocate at least half a day. This gives you time to move beyond the main shrine to the adjacent Southern Suburbs Garden (南郊公园) and the Tomb of Liu Xiang (刘湘墓), which offer a quieter atmosphere. * 🧱 The Red Walls: The famous "Red Wall Alley" (红墙夹道) is genuinely beautiful—the contrast between the vermilion walls and the green bamboo is perfect for photography.⭐⭐⭐⭐ * 🗣️ Language Barrier: Note that English explanations on the exhibits are sparse. You may need to rely on visual appreciation or a translation app for context. Verdict: A significant landmark that demands time and patience. Go early, plan for a half-day, and you’ll enjoy it much more than we managed to.

A beautifully preserved tribute to the historical figures of the Three Kingdoms period. Located within a lush park setting, the complex features traditional architecture, intricate stone carvings, and tranquil gardens that reflect the architectural style.

Massive park with lots to see, do, and eat! Navigation: get dropped off at the Jinli Main Gate (first picture). From here, you'll be greeted with lots of souvenir stores. If you want to go straight to the shrine, follow the path til you see the pagoda with the open second floor (second picture) then take a hard left. The entrance with the ticket booth is for Wu Hou Shrine. We made the mistake of going through the pagoda which took us all the way around the outside of Wu Hou shrine. When we finally circled back to it, we missed the cut off to enter. All around the shrine are a lot of free sites and food stalls. The sites include a tomb of a famous general and an area that houses stone carvings of warriors from the Song Dynasty.

A must visit for 3 Kingdoms fans. The shine have the original statues from a couple of hundred of years ago. Massive walking street outside which is kept clean which hundreds of food stalls, drinks stalls or retail.

Wuhou Shrine in Chengdu has evolved into a cohesive and structured park, combining three previously separate areas. The site offers a rich historical narrative, featuring Liu Bei, Zhuge Liang, and other figures, alongside modern, interactive displays that attract younger visitors. Red walls and traditional architecture provide iconic photo spots, while tea corners and leisure areas create a calm pace for exploration. Guides are available at the entrance for a reasonable price, though their explanations may feel rigid. Performances and small activities enhance the experience without overwhelming it. Visiting requires at least two hours to fully appreciate the content and layout. Overall, it is a thoughtful balance of history, culture, and contemporary engagement.

A great place to visit if you are interested in Shu history during the three kingdoms period. Was surprised to see that the statue of Zhao Yun not in armour despite being the first along the generals corridor.

Quite a big place to visit, especially if you like the nature, it can be made at the time with the connected Jinli old street. Just don't forget your passport if you're a foreigner and you don't have yet bought a ticket.

Chengdu Wuhou Shrine: A Historic Site of Three Kingdoms Located at 231 Wuhouci Avenue in Chengdu, the Chengdu Wuhou Shrine is a remarkable ancient temple with a deep connection to Chinese history. Surrounded by beautiful natural scenery, the site offers a blend of historical significance and serene beauty. The shrine is closely tied to the story of the Three Kingdoms, making it a must-visit for anyone interested in this period. I was very excited to visit this place and was not disappointed. The site is not just a historical monument; it also offers a vibrant local experience. There was a market with plenty of delicious local food, adding a wonderful culinary dimension to the visit. While most local people don’t speak much English, it’s easy to get by. The students are able to speak and communicate in English, and everyone I met was kind and friendly, which made for a very welcoming experience.

A must-visit for any history enthusiast, especially fans of the Three Kingdoms era! The Wuhou Shrine offers a rich dive into the legacy of Zhuge Liang and other legendary figures. The grounds are beautifully maintained, with plenty of photo-worthy spots, from ancient statues to traditional architecture. It’s a great mix of culture, history, and aesthetics. Give yourself at least 1-2 hours to explore everything. Highly recommended for both history geeks and casual visitors alike!

Entrance is free for the elderly above 60 years old. It's a historical place to get to know & learn about Liu Bei & his other generals and ministers. A good place for learning if you're a student in 🇨🇳. As for tourists, I don't really see the interesting part of this place. It's also very crowded as there's many school tours going on.

If you are a fan of the “Romance of the Three Kingdoms” the book, the TV series or the computer game, you’ll be in for a treat here. Otherwise you might just want to read about it (a summary because there were so many characters and stories) before you visit this Shrine. I’m Singaporean Chinese so I’m familiar with some of the famous war stories (military strategies) but they were not depicted in this shrine here.

This shrine honors Zhuge Liang, Liu Bei, and other key figures from the Three Kingdoms era. With its ancient cypress trees, traditional architecture, serene gardens, and historical relics, it’s a must-visit for history buffs. Take your time to soak in its deep historical significance. It's a gateway into China’s legendary past.

For those loving the romance of the three kingdoms, this is a shrine that kept the history alive, showcasing the different characters from the three kingdoms era. Huge place and travelers can takes lots of photos here or admire the nature and fauna.
The shrine is part of a larger cultural complex that includes the Temple of Liu Bei, the Shu Han emperor, and the Jinli Ancient Street nearby. There are many shops inside.
Such a cool temple … had a very calming feel and lots of space to wander and explore. The temples are beautiful and well marked that you can really feel the history.

Easily can spent 2-3hrs here if you are a fan of the three kingdom. Pay for the guide standing outside with it dedicated earpiece that costs rmb 20 per pax. Very reasonable for a detailed explaination- of course you must be able to understand mandarin
It's a nice museum to visit. It's about 三国时期, mainly about zhu ge liang (诸葛亮). It's worth to visit and more understanding about the history

A good place to learn about the popular Shu kingdom history. It is a large ground and there are many things to see. There is also Jinli street just beside the park (not part of it) where you can get food and check out the shops. Do check it out as well!

Chengdu's Wuhou Museum is a treasure trove of history intertwined with serene gardens, making it perfect for a leisurely walk. Dive into the Three Kingdoms' era while enjoying a peaceful stroll. Highly recommended!

Important historical site of ancient China. View artifacts from the Shu Kingdom and learn more about personalities from that period. Liu Bei's tomb is also located here. Many picturesque spots suitable for Instagram. One particular area which stood out was an alley with red walls and bambo grove. Recommended for fans of Romance of the three kingdoms.

If you are a fan of China history, especially the three kingdom like me, you will surely have to visit this place where history has come alive. All the while, we have read stories (or in history books) about the three kingdom, also having watched the TV serials and movies about it, what is better than personally coming by to see the real artifacts, displays and figures on display. There are so many things to see and you will feel that you have traveled back in time to the then era! I like the back gardens (peach gardens) where you can see the beautiful peach trees with flowers, the figurines of the three sworn brothers and the founding, prosperiy and demise of the Shu kingdom. Very detailed and realistic and generally if you are a fan and want to have a sight of everything, you will need simply a day. For me, due to the rushing schedule, I only spent about 2~3 hrs here before heading to the next destination but it's surely worth visiting. The admission is RMB 50 and seniors from local, macao or taiwan, aged 60years and above can enter free with the show of identity card or passport.

An splendid place if you love the ancient Chinese history and stories about the three kingdoms in Han dynasty, especiallyabout the famous military strategist Zhuge Liang. There is a plenty of history and culture to see with detailed explanation in multiple languages. You can also hire a guided tour for more in-depth understanding of the individual historical figures and the architecture. A must-go for every history lover.
Dated old shrines to worship few prominent historical figures from the 3 kingdoms period. To really appreciate the history and architecture, maybe better to hire a guide.

Wuhou Shrine is an unique shrine that houses temples of both of Zhuge Liang and Liu Bei, Liu Bei's tomb. It is the only combined memorial temple for both a king and his minister in China. It is one of the most influential site of "three kingdoms" and a must go if you are a big fan of the Romance of Three Kingdoms. The red walls are insta-famous.

Before I get into the review of 武侯祠，I had to give a thumbs up for Chengdu Tourism Administration— they did good job setting up direct bus among tourists sites. ¥10 get you to many places. And this is the first stop. All tourists sights have Wechat intro you can scan and then listen to. After visited this place, I felt like all my reading on Three Countries (三国演义) came to reality here. The friendship, royalty, dreams and legacy of those leaders and warriors all presented here like a vivid movie. A must see!

It's not only interesting, but fun too because of all the shops in this Chinese-old-styled historical place. Please correct me if I got the wrong photos but this place is what the personal tour guide told me.
A place to understand the history of 刘备 张飞 关羽 and 诸葛亮. Interesting place where you will spend about an hour there. Beside the place, there are also alley of shopping and eateries places to visit.
Interesting historical place with variuos activities and varieties of food and beverages. Although the price and hygiene is not so good, there are lovely snacks for young people.

Know the story of the 3 kingdom? Legends of Liu Bei and Chu Ke Liang? Well this is where it all ends. A temple complex dedicated to these guys.. A well conserved historical site that's a must visit. Wonder around the gardens, soak in the ambience and try to grasp some of the history and heritage from China's past. Thrilled to find the tomb of Liu Bei actually still exist on site.. That's deep! 😃
If you love the story of the Three Kingdoms and are moved by everyone in that era, this place is well worth visiting.
A very wondeful experience to walk back in time to have someone explaining the history of the Three Kingdoms and the life of Liu Bei and his 2 sworn brothers, my favourite Guan Yu.

Nice place to go, it's an archeology site of the Three Kingdoms, also have a nice garden at the back. Be prepared to walk a lot thou, the area is pretty big. Ticket is 50 Yuan for foreigner (2019 price)
We paid for a guide and it’s well worth it! What a great way to learn about the ancient history of this region and appreciate the unique architecture!
Ancient relics and artifacts are well preserved but it's just a common shrine for those who are not interested in the history of Three Kingdom and the heroes of Shu kingdom.
Interesting place to learn more about the three kingdoms and have a nice walk in pretty (not spectacular) gardens. Located near a tourist shopping street. They charge a fee for admission.

Three Kingdoms fans, this is the place to go. See the grave or tomb of Liu Bei. I was surprised to learn that it apparently has never been robbed because he was buried with nothing pf value. Wonderful scenery everywhere. The bamboo corridor was an unexpected treat.
Go early to pay your respects and remember the most famous strategist in China history- Zhugeliang and his team- Liu Bei, Zhao Yun and Guan Yu.
Really impress with this place. Has lots of historical sites and information. Surrounding areas has lots of shops in traditional setting. Can spend about 3 hours here.
A place you must visit if you ever read Chinese novel Legend of Three Kingdoms and you know Zhugeliang.
A really nice place to slow down with friends and a cup of tea under the bamboo clusters. Then ajorn next door to the touristy spot JinLi for some local street food.
I went there a week before Chinese open semester, then I faced a huge crowd of people. You need to buy the ticket
Super nice place. The bamboo Forrest and red walls are iconic. Have to visit if u come Chengdu

Visit the shrine on Saturday so there were too many domestic tourists. Because the shrine is being repaired, there are some rooms not for sightseeing. Public toilets only have 3 rooms and are very dirty.
It is a ancient shrine to memorize Zhuguliang and Liubei of Three Kingdoms period in ancient China
If you loved the Shu Kingdom. Be sure to visit the Liu Bei and Zhang Liang Museum

Just a bit crowded during summer time and hot. It's a shrine of a very significant figure in Chinese history and the story of Wu Hou (Zhu Ge Liang) is well known throughout Asia including Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia.
A very interesting place and all the surroundings and little streets are fantastic. I imagine that at night it will be better.
Beautiful place. Didn’t get a chance to get in. It was closed when we arrived. But the park was open to the public to visit.
Very touristic and too much crowds when I went there but there's many valuable history you can scout.
A beautiful shrine, near a great area for shopping, snacks, and beautiful architecture. We took many many pictures while visiting. Highly recommended!

Very convenient to buy a ticket from the counter. It is an interesting museum for people interested in the 3 kingdom. Guided tour is not necessary unless you want to understand in detail. Spent around 2h+ at the area. The exit is conveniently located at the food street of JinLi.
This place has a lot of history to tell, but might be hard for foreign visitors to appreciate since you really need to know the history to understand what they are all about.
Recommended place to visit for one who love the "romance of the three kingdoms".
Historical place and very beautiful botanic garden inside. Free wifi and guide if you understand Chinese.
Overall better experience than the small alleys experience. Relaxed and peaceful.
An incredible hidden jewel in the sichuan country side. Delightful decor and tastiest sichuan specialities.

Avery nice temple, there are lessons to be learned from this temple, about the glory of the three dynasties in this area. There are many food and drink vendors near the temple, and there are some good spots for photos.

A nice temple with plenty of huge crowds and lots of local Chinese tourists arriving by the busloads that are loud and obnoxious... they seem to be from the smaller villages and act like uncouth hillbillies with no class. Avoid them like the plague and the scum they are. Go early to avoid these insect scum and enjoy the place to yourself before it's overrun by these locals.
Nice grounds, but lots of people when we were there. Still good to have somewhere like this in the middle of chengdu. Watch out for the road crossing just outside, it can be tricky.

It was really lovely with a ton of Chengdu specialties for food choices throughout the shrine. Lots of traditional areas to view. There are really nice classic shows you must watch but be careful of overpricing! You should wait and see your options. Really worth it to see!

If you're familiar with the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, this is a shrine dedicated to the heroes of that time. Wu Hou is actually Zhuge Liang. Nice place if you want to read a little more history. There are statues of each hero and English descriptions of their background. There is also a mausoleum where some of them were supposedly buried. The garden within the shrine features numerous bonsai in all sorts of shapes.
Very beautiful and peaceful garden with many paths to follow and different ambiances to discover.

Nice place to visit if it's your first time, the statues and artifacts are very well preserved. Interesting for anyone who wants to find out more about Wu Hou and the important people during the three kingdoms
A very nice hotel (Terra Hotel), the people are nice and friendly. The coffee and food are very good.

I love reading novel <The Three Kingdoms> since I was a child. I always admire the heroes in ancient China and characters in the novel who were loyal and determined to their dreams and vows. Especially the military counsellor Liang Zhuge and general Yu Guan.Both of them were like role models to today Chinese and still been worshipped till now. The Shrine brought me back Han Dynasty which was 2000 years ago, it is good to see history.
Ancient Chinese Temple. Well preserved. It houses a Bonsai garden. Nearby is Jinli Street. Famous for it's large variety of Chinese Street food. But be ready for very strong odours and a large crowd.
Memorial place for Three Sworn Brothers in Three Kingdom Story. Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei. And also their intelligent advisor Zhuge Liang.

I have been visiting shrines and temples in Japan and Korea, and even though this was a big shrine, there were little to no information about the shrine. I even got the audio guide, which was utterly useless, it didn't provide any relevant information and was difficult to work with. Also, some information was clearly translated without any supervusion, as the numbers or the fact didn't match history. It was unbelievable how little effort was given to provide info in English here. Do Not get the audio guide, you are better off with Wikipedia and Google.
Beautiful historic shrine with scenic gardens, I spent an afternoon there on a sunny Monday and really enjoyed it.
Wu Hou Shrine is one of greatest places to see the Three Kingdoms Story. And hot tourist spot, JinLi street, is located just near by the Shrine.
If you can read chinese fluently and understand the charscters and history of the 3 kingdoms, this place should be on your bucket list. Didnt see any audio guides, especially in english.
Main attraction are human statues with their story line. About the famous heroes from the 3 kingdoms
The souvenir inside are so expensive, it's better to go shopping to shop outside.

2 kilometers away from my alma matet, I am on a MBA progran in USA，but I miss a lot about Chengdu:college life,history,food,you name It.One of the best memory in my life imprinted here.I also recommend guys to vist:Dufu thatched cottage,jinlin alley,Wenshu monastery,chunxi street.you will regret if you miss them.
Just beside jinli pedestrian street. Good to visit as it is a significant historical site. Nice gardens and bonsai.
well, my son was so anxious to go there, and was a bit disappointed by the statues of Kongming and Zhao Yun. you reallyneed to know the history well to understand this place.
Very interesting shrine devoted to the heroes of the Shu in the Three Kingdoms period. Try to find Liu Bei's son!
Full of people, interesting and beatiful but not worth the steep price (of 50 yuan if I remember correctly)
If you like a bit of history other than just the spicy food in Chengdu, this has to be on the list of your must see sights.
Very interesting place to visit. Will recommend to get a audio or guide to explain the entire set up.
Do sign up for audio tour or guided tour for very informative tour of the shrine

這次來成都旅遊，順道過來「武侯祠」走走。這裡整體的氛圍蠻沉穩的，紅牆搭配翠綠的竹林，確實很有古色古香的韻味，尤其是那面經典的紅牆夾道，隨便拍幾張照都很有意境。雖然是對三國歷史的紀念地，但就算不深究歷史，單純在園林裡散散步、看看古建築，整體的感覺也挺不錯。 園區的維護做得很好，動線規劃也算順暢。這裡和隔壁的錦里連在一起，逛完幽靜的祠堂可以直接去隔壁感受熱鬧的市井氣息，這種一靜一動的體驗還蠻有趣的。雖然觀光客不少，但因為空間夠大，找個安靜的角落坐一下，感受那種厚重的歷史感，還是能讓人放鬆下來。 服務設施挺完善的，指標也很清楚。對我來說，這裡不需要帶著那種「必看什麼」的壓力，就是個適合下午過來晃晃、感受一下老成都人文氣息的地方。如果你對歷史有一點興趣，或者只是想找個有美感的地方走走，這裡算是個挺值得偶爾過來回味的景點。

2019年に三国志好きの友達と四川を訪れました。 蜀と言えば成都、劉備や諸葛亮が治めていた地をこの目で見たかったからです。 この武侯祠は三国志好きははずせないでしょうね。 現地では今でも蜀は愛されてるなと感じました。 訪れたタイミングも我ながら絶妙でしたね。 何か月後に新型コロナ、それも中国から広がりましたからね。 ここ何年か日中関係もよくないですしね。 昔の三国志のように義を重んじるようになってほしい。

촉한의 수도였던 청두에, 제갈량의 시호인 '무후'를 따서 이름붙인 청두무후사. 본래 제갈량의 사당이지만 유비의 묘가 함께 위치해 있습니다. 삼국지의 영웅서사에 가슴 뛰었던 분들이 청두에 오셨다면, 반드시 방문해야 하는 성지 입니다. 하지만 그 명성에 비해 대단한 볼거리를 갖춘것은 아니니 너무 기대하지 않는 것이 좋습니다. 한가지 좋은점은 곳곳에 한글 설명이 함께 있다는 것인데요. 그만큼 한국에서 삼국지의 위상이 높기 때문이 아닐까 짐작해 봅니다. 참고로 입장료는 50위안이고 여권이 필요하구요. 무후사 바로 옆에 위치한 금리 Jinli old street도 함께 방문하시면 좋습니다.

Ho visitato il Tempio di Wu Hou a Chengdu questa mattina e devo dire che è un luogo molto interessante e grande, con giardini ben curati e bonsai affascinanti. All'interno del tempio c'è anche un museo che vale la pena visitare. Tuttavia, ho riscontrato alcuni problemi che hanno un po' rovinato la mia esperienza. Innanzitutto, il percorso da seguire all'interno del tempio non è per niente chiaro, anzi, è molto confuso. Non c'è una mappa dettagliata o indicazioni sufficienti per aiutare i turisti a orientarsi. Quando ho chiesto informazioni all'entrata, ho avuto difficoltà a trovare qualcuno che parlasse inglese, il che ha reso le cose ancora più difficili. Inoltre, la folla di turisti cinesi può essere molto rumorosa e confusionaria. Sono spesso più interessati a scattare selfie che a rispettare gli altri visitatori, e possono essere piuttosto fastidiosi. Purtroppo, non sono riuscito a godermi al meglio la visita di questo tempio a causa di questi problemi. In generale, consiglio di visitare il Tempio di Wu Hou, ma di essere preparati a una certa confusione.

이 곳의 이름은 촉한의 승상 제갈량의 시호를 딴 무후사이지만 소열황제 유비의 릉이 있는 곳입니다. 삼국지연의의 매니아들이라면 청두에 와서 반드시 방문하시길 권해드립니다. 아래 몇가지 주의사항을 참고하시면 되겠습니다. 1. 트립닷컴을 통해 예약을 하신 경우 입구 기준 좌측을 둘러보시면 지류 티켓을 발권할 수 있는 곳이 있어, 발권 후 입장하시면 됩니다. 2. 내부로 라이터 등 화기를 가져갈 수 없습니다. 흡연자이신 경우 당황하지 마시고 일단 라이터를 반납하신 후 관람 후 나와 라이터를 반납한 통으로 다시 가셔서 반납하신 라이터보다 더 좋은 것 하나를 찾아가시면 되겠습니다. 진짜 비싼 라이터라면 직원에게 따로 보관요청을 하셔야 합니다.

思ったより 楽しかった ​成都武侯祠は、**中国の三国時代（蜀漢）の英雄たちを祀る、非常に歴史的な価値の高い祠堂（しどう）**です。 ​⛩️ 武侯祠の概要 ​所在地: 中国 四川省 成都市 武侯区 ​祀られている人物: ​諸葛亮（しょかつりょう）：蜀漢の宰相。「武侯」は諸葛亮が没後に贈られた諡号（しごう）「忠武侯（ちゅうぶこう）」に由来します。 ​劉備（りゅうび）：蜀漢の初代皇帝。 ​その他、関羽・張飛をはじめとする蜀漢の功臣たち。 ​最大の特徴: 中国国内で唯一、君主（劉備）と臣下（諸葛亮）が一体となって祀られている祠堂である点です。このため、「三国聖地」とも呼ばれ、世界的に影響力のある三国志遺跡博物館となっています。

20251024成都武侯祠，位於中華人民共和國四川省成都市南門武侯祠大街，是中國唯一的君臣合祀祠廟，由武侯祠、漢昭烈廟及惠陵組成，人們習慣將三者統稱為武侯祠。成都武侯祠始建於公元223年修建惠陵（劉備的陵寢）之時，其中武侯祠（諸葛亮的專祠）建於唐以前，初與祭祀劉備（漢昭烈帝）的漢昭烈廟相鄰，明朝初年重建時將武侯祠併入，形成了君臣合祀，祠堂與陵園合一的格局。除惠陵以外現存祠廟主體建築為1672年清康熙年間復建。1984年成立成都武侯祠博物館，2008年被評為首批國家一級博物館。 成都武侯祠博物館現分為三國歷史遺蹟區（又稱文物區，由漢昭烈廟、武侯祠、惠陵、三義廟等組成）、西區（以劉湘陵園為主體）、錦里民俗區三大部分，面積15萬平方米[1]。2006年武侯祠被評為國家AAAA級旅遊景區，是全中國影響最大的三國遺蹟博物館 需購票進入~有個紅牆務必打卡拍照

地點很不錯，很大的地方可以走很久，也保有一些三國遺跡、遺物。位於四川省成都市武侯區武侯祠大街231號，開放時間5月1日-10月31日：8：00-20：00；11月1日-4月30日：8：00-18：30。 武侯祠占地15萬平方米，始建于章武三年（223年），原是紀念諸葛亮的專祠，亦稱孔明廟、諸葛祠、丞相祠等，後合併為君臣合祀祠廟。明洪武二十四年（1391年），蜀獻王朱椿對武侯祠和漢昭烈廟進行了一次全面的修繕和整合，廢除原在漢昭烈廟西側的武侯祠，把諸葛亮像移入漢昭烈廟內劉備像東側，關羽、張飛像排列於西。四川的官吏將北地王劉諶、諸葛亮之子諸葛瞻和鎮守關口格鬥而死的傅僉也陪祀廟內。 武侯祠是民眾對蜀漢丞相諸葛亮“鞠躬盡瘁死而後已”精神的肯定和讚譽的載體，也是三國遺跡源頭，由漢昭烈廟、武侯祠、惠陵、三義廟四部分組成，屬於成都武侯祠博物館的文化遺產保護區。

武侯祠是成都的文化地标，地铁3号线武侯祠站下，走5分钟就到，导航精准。票价50元，学生半价，停车位少，建议坐地铁或公交，附近共享单车也方便。景区古朴典雅，红墙绿瓦间透着三国气息。进门先看到诸葛亮殿，金光闪闪的塑像庄严肃穆，刘备墓在后面，周围古树环绕，安静得让人肃然起敬。展厅里文物丰富，石碑、匾额和三国故事讲解牌很详细，像上了一堂历史课。 人多时有点挤，尤其是节假日和周末，拍照得抢位置，建议工作日早上来，清净又舒服。园子不算大，慢慢逛1-2小时够了，厕所分布合理，干净整洁，服务员态度亲切，导览牌清晰。旁边锦里有各种小吃，串串和担担面超香，武侯祠内小卖部东西贵，水10元一瓶，推荐自带水和零食。买的茶叶和茶具还有手工艺品还行。 春季和秋季来最合适，樱花或银杏配红墙超美，夏天太热，带防晒霜和帽子。门票网上订省时间，现场排队慢。适合三国迷、历史爱好者或带小孩来学知识。唯一小遗憾是热门点人多，拍全景得耐心等。总之，武侯祠是成都必打卡的地方，历史底蕴深厚，风景也不错，五星推荐，下次还想再来细品！ *Tips*: 早到避高峰，带现金有些摊位不收卡，锦里吃饭别错过麻辣小吃。

成都武侯祠是纪念刘备、诸葛亮等蜀汉英雄人物庙宇所在。它肇始于蜀汉昭烈帝章武元年（221年）刘备惠陵修建时，在修建惠陵的同时也修建了汉昭烈庙。约在公元500年前后南北朝时期，武侯祠从成都“少城”迁建惠陵、汉昭烈庙旁，这格局持续到明代。明洪武二十三年（1390年），明蜀献王朱椿到武侯祠朝拜，以“君臣宜为一体”为由，将惠陵、汉昭烈庙、武侯祠合为一体，由于诸葛亮在老百姓心目中的影响超过刘备，民间习惯称为“武侯祠”。明末，武侯祠毁于战火，清康熙十年（1671年），在旧址上恢复重建武侯祠，形成现在所见格局。1961年武侯祠被国务院公布为全国第一批重点文物保护单位，1984年成立博物馆，1997年三义庙整体搬迁至武侯祠，2003年成都南郊公园与武侯祠合并，2004年10月锦里正式对外开放，2008年武侯祠被评为国家一级博物馆，2009年1月锦里二期开肆。武侯祠现占地15万平方米（230亩），由三国文化遗产保护区 、三国文化体验区（即西区，原南郊公园）和锦里民俗区三部分组成。作为全国唯一的君臣合祀祠庙和最负盛名的诸葛亮、刘备及蜀汉英雄纪念地及全世界影响最大的三国遗迹博物馆，武侯祠享有“三国圣地”之美誉，年平均接待观众约1000万人次。
